summary: Someone just failed to log into this computer

context.what_happened: A Windows login attempt was rejected — wrong password or unknown user

ai_response.title: Someone just failed to log into this computer with an incorrect password.
ai_response.what_happened: A Windows login attempt was rejected because of a wrong password or unknown user. This is the second time today someone has tried to access your account without success.
ai_response.why_risky: This could be a sign that someone is trying to guess your password, which can lead to unauthorized access and potentially serious consequences, such as stolen files or identity theft.
how_to_prevent: Use a strong, unique password for your Windows account
Enable Windows account lockout policy to lock after 5 wrong attempts
Disable Remote Desktop (RDP) if remote access is not needed
ai_response.learning_tip: If you notice repeated failed login attempts, it's likely a brute-force attack. Review event viewer and consider changing your password immediately.

summary: Windows Defender real-time protection was just turned off

context.why_this_is_serious: Your computer is now unprotected from viruses and malware
context.message: Windows Defender real-time monitoring was disabled.

event_data.message: Windows Defender real-time monitoring was disabled.

ai_response.title: Windows Defender real-time protection was just turned off.
ai_response.what_happened: Your Windows Defender real-time monitoring was disabled, leaving your computer unprotected from viruses and malware. This means any file you open or website you visit can be scanned by nothing, allowing malware to execute freely without detection.
ai_response.why_risky: This is serious because your computer is now vulnerable to infections that can steal your personal data, compromise your online accounts, or even take control of your device. As the attacker's goal is often to disable Defender as their first step, this is a classic indicator of an active infection or a compromised administrator account.
how_to_prevent: Re-enable real-time protection immediately: Start → Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → turn on.
Do not download or open anything until protection is restored.
Check if any software 'required' you to disable it — that software is malicious.
If you cannot re-enable it, run the Windows Defender Offline scan from a restart.
ai_response.learning_tip: Be cautious of repeated patterns like USB devices being plugged in multiple times. This could be an indication of malware activity.
